comment: Raises the two Uranium Expanded metals to end-game tiers: ferrous uranium to 5 (anvil tier 4, alongside
stainless steel) and uranium steel to 7 (anvil tier 6, the top of the ladder). That mod ships them at 3 and 4,
level with iron and steel.
Why a whole asset file rather than a JSON patch. An anvil does not carry a tier of its own - BlockAnvil.OnLoaded
looks its metal up in SurvivalCoreSystem.metalsByCode and copies that metal's tier, leaving 0 when the lookup
misses. That table is built once, in AssetsLoaded, as
GetMany<MetalProperty>(logger, 'worldproperties/block/metal.json', null)
with a null domain, so EVERY domain's copy of this path is read, and each variant is assigned by code:
metalsByCode[variant.Code.Path] = variant
An assignment, not an add - so a second file naming the same metal replaces the first, which is exactly what
this file does. No patch, no array index, no dependence on which mod's patches ran first.
Patching game:worldproperties/block/metal.json instead does NOT work, and several shapes of it were tried:
Uranium Expanded appends its metals with '/variants/-', so they sit at an index that only exists after that
mod's patches run, and Haft sorts earlier. Targeting /variants/23/tier errored outright from patches/, and
silently changed nothing from compatibility/. Forcing load order with a modinfo dependency moved Haft last and
still left the table holding vanilla's 23 entries.
This file is deliberately NOT under compatibility/uraniumexpanded/: assets there overwrite a file the mod
already ships at the same path, and Haft ships none, so a copy placed there is never read. Loading
unconditionally costs two unused entries in metalsByCode when Uranium Expanded is absent - nothing references
them, because the ingots, items and anvil variants all come from that mod or from its gated patch.
Stainless steel and titanium need no entry here: they are vanilla metals that already carry tiers 5 and 6, and
their anvils pick those up through the same OnLoaded lookup with no help from Haft.
